scope: Pinned initialization/consumption argument for the two typed primitive families; not a proof of destination or island/thread state.
findings: Inverter cached input starts as Z and its destination starts null. A changed port-zero input updates the cache and sets the destination before scheduling; further input updates coalesce into that pending event.

Static part-select bounds initialize in the base constructor. A received vector is sliced into val_ before scheduling with a non-null destination. Its empty default vector is not read as initialized elements.

Both run_run methods save the destination locally and clear the pending destination before sending their cached result. Paused queued-event inspection covers initialized state; neither method itself yields to SPICE.

Protected-base adjustment is performed within the owning constructor, using an explicit generic-event key. The observer uses that registry rather than guessing offsets or casting arbitrary event payloads.
The transmission-gate island requires separate mesh, port, filter and branch contracts; this observer does not cover it.
